repositories.brief_summary: RISC-V frame pointers and arm64 store-release codegen landed, while atomic-record-field discussion and a fiber-cache-leak fix moved forward.
repositories.new_features_summary: RISC-V frame pointer support, arm64 store-release barrier codegen, `caml_program` startup loop, and a `Gc.stat` doc fix merged to trunk.
repositories.new_features:
- Frame pointer support for the **RISC-V (riscv64) Linux** backend, adding `emit_store_word_with_barrier`-style prologue/epilogue handling and configure-time detection, by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([#14506](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14506))
- On **arm64**, mutable-field-assignment write barriers now emit a store-release (`stlr`, or `stlur` when `FEAT_LRCPC2` is available) instead of `dmb ishld; str`, with older cores (Cortex-A53/-A57/-A72/-A73) kept on the fenced path and the default chosen at configure time, by [Sebastian Pop](https://github.com/sebpop) and Xavier Leroy ([#14922](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14922))
- `caml_program` is now generated as a **loop over a table of module entry points** instead of one call block per module, making startup code size independent of the number of linked modules, by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) and Pierre Oechsel ([#13217](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13217))
- Fixed `-dtypedtree` output incorrectly printing `Twith_modtypesubst` as `Twith_modtype`, by [Corentin De Souza](https://github.com/fantazio) ([#14932](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14932))
- Documentation for `Gc.stat` corrected to state that `stack_size` (unlike `heap_chunks`, `free_blocks`, and `largest_free`) is now populated again in OCaml 5.5, by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([#14942](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14942))
- Memory-model manual documentation clarified on how domain-frontier updates behave, by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) ([#14924](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14924))

repositories.discussions_summary: Debate over how atomic record fields should behave under functional updates, plus Option/Result combinator naming and bigarray Memprof gaps.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- Whether **functional record updates that implicitly copy atomic fields** should be forbidden or should perform an implicit atomic read: [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported the missing atomic load ([#14918](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14918)); [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) opened a PR to forbid the pattern citing OxCaml's precedent ([#14931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14931)), but after further discussion with [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli), and [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) concluded that record updates are more constrained than pattern-matching (fields are read exactly once, unconditionally), so [#14931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14931) was closed in favor of [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)'s alternative that implicitly performs the atomic read ([#14935](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14935))
- A related question on the **unspecified evaluation order** of fields in `{ r with ... }` record-update expressions, raised by [Guillaume Bury](https://github.com/Gbury), which [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) linked to the atomic-field discussion above ([#14129](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14129), [#14918](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14918), [#14931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14931))
- [Michael Neumann](https://github.com/mneumann)'s request for point-free `{Option,Result}.andthen`/`orelse` combinators was closed by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli), who explained the stdlib team's preference for a `try_value`-style combinator (previously discussed in [#13937](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13937)) over `andthen`/`orelse`, after which Neumann agreed and opened [#14941](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14941) implementing `try_value` ([#14893](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14893))
- [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) raised that `Gc.Memprof` does not track the lifetime of **bigarray subarrays**, causing memory-profiling tools like memtrace to underestimate live memory in applications such as Mirage ([#14938](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14938))
- [Sebastian Pop](https://github.com/sebpop) and [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) debated whether the PLDI'18 *Bounding Data Races in Space and Time* compilation scheme's fences around AArch64 atomic RMWs are stronger than necessary, backed by herd7 litmus tests distinguishing LSE and LL/SC atomic forms ([#14936](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14936))
- [Chet Murthy](https://github.com/chetmurthy) reported that `Scanf.unescaped` accepts hex (`\x41`) but rejects octal (`\o101`) escapes, which [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) confirmed matches the documented spec but agreed is surprising behavior ([#14930](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14930))
repositories.trends_summary: Continued focus on memory-model precision across architectures and on tightening atomics semantics in the type system and runtime.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Multiple concurrent efforts to **refine low-level memory-ordering guarantees**: arm64 store-release barrier codegen ([#14922](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14922)), dropping redundant AArch64 RMW fences ([#14936](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14936)), and updated memory-model documentation for domain frontiers ([#14924](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14924), [#14134](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14134))
- Growing attention to **atomic record fields interacting with existing language features** (functional updates, pattern matching, evaluation order), spanning [#14918](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14918), [#14931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14931), [#14935](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14935), and [#14129](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14129)
- Continued **cross-architecture portability work** landing frame-pointer support architecture by architecture, following RISC-V this week ([#14506](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14506)) with POWER proposed in parallel ([#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14505))
- Runtime portability fixes are increasingly driven by **libc and platform edge cases** reported by external users (musl on Intel CPUs in [#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14933), Haiku in [#14773](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14773), Cygwin in [#14921](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14921))

repositories.brief_summary: opam 2.6.0~alpha1 was released, bundling .install file `root`/`rootexec` sections, `--ignore-available-on`, and several disk-usage and Windows fixes.
repositories.new_features_summary: The 2.6.0~alpha1 release adds `--ignore-available-on`, `.install` `root`/`rootexec` sections, and disk-space and Windows fixes.
repositories.new_features:
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) tagged and merged the **2.6.0~alpha1 release** ([#7046](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7046)), consolidating the CHANGES file with the accumulated feature and bug-fix list for the upcoming 2.6 line.
- [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian) added the `--ignore-available-on` CLI **option** to allow ignoring a package's `available:` field, with reftests covering the new `OPAMIGNOREAVAILABLE` environment variable ([#6836](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6836), fixes [#5283](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5283)).
- [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian) and [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) added `root` and `rootexec` **sections to `.install` files**, letting packages install files to arbitrary prefix-root paths without relying on `..` ([#6938](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6938), fixes [#6919](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6919)).
- [Kayo Tei](https://github.com/tuesdayjz) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) improved `opam init --bare` **performance** by skipping default-compiler selection entirely for bare inits, adding a `?no_compiler` argument to `OpamClient.init` ([#6957](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6957), fixes [#5815](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5815)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) reduced **disk usage** by having the internal `sources` directory cache only dev packages instead of every package, removing it after the build phase (24% speedup reported on a benchmark) ([#6440](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6440), fixes [#4056](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/4056), [#5448](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5448)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) further cut **disk usage** by removing a package's build directory as soon as possible after installation rather than waiting until the whole command finishes ([#6906](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6906), fixes [#5884](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5884)).
- [Stephen Sherratt](https://github.com/gridbugs) changed the shell **env hook** to update the current bin path in `PATH` in place instead of always prioritising opam's path over every other one ([#6859](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6859), fixes [#6815](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6815)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) reordered the **list of actions** shown to users by increased priority for install/upgrade/remove commands ([#6864](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6864), fixes [#6863](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6863)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) made `opam init` show a working `opam switch create` **command** when it fails to create the default switch ([#6851](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6851)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) fixed **package installation** during `opam pin add <url to archive>`, broken since 2.3.0~alpha1 ([#7012](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7012), fixes [#6999](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6999)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) fixed `opam lock` support for **dependency formulas** that include disjunctions ([#6990](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6990), fixes [#6944](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6944)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) fixed the filename check used when parsing arguments so `/` is recognised as a **directory separator on Windows** ([#6981](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6981), fixes [#6940](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6940)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) and [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) re-allowed `.install` files containing `..`, now with a warning (error under strict mode) instead of a hard failure, and stopped the installer from creating unnecessary intermediate directories for such paths ([#7008](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7008), [#7015](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7015)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) enabled detection of installed packages via their **virtual names** on ALT Linux, RHEL-based and SUSE-based distributions ([#6431](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6431), fixes [#6426](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6426)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) improved the error message of `opam pin list` when a pinned package's internal source directory doesn't exist ([#6597](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6597)).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) made opam's `git` calls more **deterministic** regardless of the user's global or system git config, and fetched repositories now use a deterministically-named `main` branch instead of following `init.defaultBranch` ([#6992](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6992), fixes [#6937](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6937)).
- [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) documented the raw-field syntax more prominently in the manual ([#6846](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6846)).

repositories.brief_summary: ocaml-lsp landed workspace-folder, Dune-promotion, and Dune-formatting fixes alongside a large TypeScript-to-OCaml e2e test migration.
repositories.new_features_summary: Fixes shipped for dynamic workspace folders, Dune promotion tracking, generated-source workspace symbols, and Dune-only formatting.
repositories.new_features:
- Clients can now add their **first workspace folder** dynamically after initialization, fixing a bug where the initial folder update was rejected ([#1747](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1747)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Fixed **Dune promotion reference counts**, unregistering promotion commands once their diagnostics are cleared so promotion actions no longer accumulate stale entries ([#1746](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1746)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Workspace symbols** for generated sources now resolve to their actual files in the `_build` directory instead of leaving them unresolved ([#1742](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1742)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), building on an earlier investigation by [Corentin Leruth](https://github.com/tatchi) ([#1097](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1097)).
- **Dune document formatting** is now restricted to actual Dune documents, so whole-document formatting requests for OCamllex, Menhir, and Cram files are no longer routed through Dune's S-expression formatter, while Menhir/OCamllex semantic-action range formatting is preserved ([#1621](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1621)) by [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto).
- Fixed a **spelling error** in ocamlformat error messages ([#1737](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1737)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).

repositories.brief_summary: LRU cache for indexing memory usage merged; Windows CI failures traced to a dune 3.24.0 regression.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `--cache-size` flag bounds ocaml-index memory usage via an LRU cache; index format version bumped.
repositories.new_features:
- New `--cache-size` command-line flag added to the `ocaml-index` binary, setting an **LRU cache** size in kb to bound memory usage in read-heavy indexing scenarios, defaulting to 1,000,000 kb (1GB), merged via [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos)'s work on [#2079](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/pull/2079)
- **Index storage format** bumped (`index_magic_number` changed from `Merl2023I004` to `Merl2023I005`), meaning previously generated `.index` files must be regenerated after upgrading ([#2079](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/pull/2079))
- **Occurrences analysis** reworked so `related_uids` lookups pass an explicit union-find store alongside each loaded index rather than merging union-find structures in place, part of the same memory-usage work ([#2079](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/pull/2079))
- Debug output for `ocaml-index` now prints LRU cache statistics when run with `--debug` ([#2079](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/pull/2079))
- `CHANGES.md` documents the new index-format memory-usage behavior under a dedicated entry ([#2079](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/pull/2079))

repositories.brief_summary: Melange 0.1 was removed for Dune 3.25, macOS gained a `sandbox-exec` backend, and process-spawning was hardened across macOS/Windows.
repositories.new_features_summary: Melange 0.1 removed in Dune 3.25 (breaking), macOS `sandbox-exec` sandboxing, OCaml runtime-event tracing, and spawn/digest-cache fixes shipped.
repositories.new_features:
- **Breaking change**: `(using melange 0.1)` is deleted starting with Dune language 3.25 — projects must migrate to `(using melange 1.0)`, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#14574](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14574))
- `--sandbox-actions` now works on macOS via a new `sandbox-exec` backend (alongside `bwrap` on Linux), denying writes to the shared cache database while preserving normal filesystem access, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15500](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15500))
- Numbers with a unit suffix now allow the unit to be omitted when the value is `0` — `dune cache trim --trimmed-size 0` and `--trimmed-size 0TiB` are equivalent — by [Reynir Björnsson](https://github.com/reynir) ([#15498](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15498))
- `dune install --dry-run` now validates non-empty destination directories as part of its checks, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15501](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15501))
- Dune now terminates all launched sub-processes even if Dune itself receives `SIGKILL`, by setting a parent-death signal on spawned children, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15483](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15483))
- Fixed the stat-based digest cache to account for `ctime`, preventing stale source digests from being served after certain filesystem changes, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15495](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15495))
- Added an OCaml runtime-events trace category: when trace collection is enabled, Dune now polls `runtime_events` at scheduler idle points and on shutdown and emits runtime phases/counters as trace events, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15468](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15468))
- Generated `bash`, `zsh`, and PowerShell completion scripts now fall back to the shell's normal filename completion when cmdliner has no semantic suggestions to offer, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) with [Puneeth Chaganti](https://github.com/punchagan) and [Ambre Austen Suhamy](https://github.com/ElectreAAS) ([#15442](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15442))
repositories.activity_summary: New PRs opened for a Landlock sandbox backend, merlin multi-mode configs, and fish completion, alongside a large spawn/process hardening push.
repositories.activity:

- [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) landed a broad **process-spawning hardening** pass: workers now connect to the action-runner over an inherited socketpair instead of dialing back to the RPC server ([#15530](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15530), noted as temporarily breaking Windows action runners), plus fixes for macOS `chdir` error reporting ([#15526](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15526)), macOS fd-count errors in tracing ([#15529](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15529)), RPC process cwd inheritance on macOS ([#15552](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15552)), premature-EOF handling in `sendfile` ([#15554](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15554), [#15553](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15553)), oversized `copyfile` path rejection ([#15527](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15527)), `ENOTDIR` treated as a missing path ([#15475](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15475)), uninitialized `wait4`/`fsevents` allocations ([#15524](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15524), [#15525](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15525)), removal of `lsof`-based fd counting ([#15477](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15477)), and preference for `Spawn`/`Proc.wait` over raw `Unix` calls ([#15538](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15538), [#15535](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15535))

- [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) fixed Melange/Merlin preprocessing configuration ([#15491](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15491), reproduced in [#15489](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15489)), staged wrapped root deps for JS emission in the sandbox ([#15376](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15376)), fixed a Melange promote-test regression ([#15492](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15492)), and exposed `repr` on `compilation_mode` ([#15487](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15487))
- Windows-specific fixes and coverage continued: [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) merged a regression test for bin-layout artifact names ([#15517](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15517)), while [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) opened `Proc.wait` support for Windows PIDs ([#15536](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15536)) and preservation of Windows flock handles/errors, reviewed by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) ([#15528](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15528))

repositories.trends_summary: Process-spawning hardening across macOS/Windows and diversification of sandboxing backends (bwrap/sandbox-exec/Landlock) were the dominant themes.
repositories.emerging_trends:

- **Sandbox-action backends are diversifying** beyond Linux `bwrap`: macOS now has `sandbox-exec` support ([#15500](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15500)) and a Landlock backend for Linux is in progress with converging independent implementations ([#15231](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15231), [#15504](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15504))

repositories.brief_summary: Merged install of `.cmx` files to fix warning 58 in client code, while relocatable-install and Windows build work continued on open PRs.
repositories.new_features_summary: ocamlfind now installs `.cmx` files for its libraries, silencing compiler warning 58 in downstream projects.
repositories.new_features:
- `ocamlfind install` now ships `.cmx` files (`findlib.cmx`, `findlib_config.cmx`, `topfind.cmx`, `fl_args.cmx`, `fl_lint.cmx`, `fl_meta.cmx`, `fl_split.cmx`, `fl_topo.cmx`, `fl_package_base.cmx`, `fl_metascanner.cmx`, `fl_metatoken.cmx`, `fl_dynload.cmx`) alongside the existing `.cmi`/`.cma`/`.cmxa` artifacts, resolving the **warning 58 [no-cmx-file]** reported by client code such as Rocq when built against Findlib ([#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120), fixing [#117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/117))
- Follow-up cleanup by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) on top of [#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120) removed `ocaml_args.cmi` from the installed file list, since `ocaml_args` is only part of the `ocamlfind` binary and never belonged in an installable library ([c9c7a70](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/commit/c9c7a707169a89fdfe607cd48ca536a68b7c8d49))
- Corrected the install list to stop referencing `topdirs.cmx`/`toploop.cmx`, which never existed in the build, and `num_top.cmx`/`num_top_printers.cmx`, which were never built for native code ([2fbe516](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/commit/2fbe5160196e15e2efc90531bb9137f1d58c73d0), [4e36b63](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/commit/4e36b63c0c35d6411103087a9e0218ef5a17aa27))
- CI configuration restored on Ubuntu by pinning explicit `default` and `archive` opam repositories in the GitHub Actions workflow ([751ae7a](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/commit/751ae7a5b906b263f523eda405f23df8fcf6dd59))
repositories.activity_summary: Three PRs remain open covering relocatable installs, Windows build fixes, and removal of `-with-relative-paths-at`, all stacked around OCaml 5.5 support.
repositories.activity:
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) opened **"Relocatable ocamlfind with sprinkles"** ([#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)), adapting ocamlfind for OCaml 5.5 and extending `findlib.conf` semantics to interpret relative paths so that installations to different prefixes for the same compiler configuration can be byte-for-byte identical, per the relocatability definition in [ocaml/RFCs#53](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/53)
- The same author reopened **Windows build fixes for MSYS2/Cygwin** directly as [#121](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/121) (superseding the earlier [#112](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/112), which was closed in favor of it), addressing a Cygwin build failure from mishandled `;` path separators, silent misgeneration of `findlib.conf` under MSYS2, and an incorrect `META.pkg` check during `ocamlfind install`
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) also opened a draft PR to **remove `-with-relative-paths-at` support** ([#123](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/123)), simplifying the codebase now that the relative-path handling is being reworked in [#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)
- [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai)'s **"Make paths from ld.conf absolute"** PR ([#119](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/119)), which fixed relative-path handling needed for the `ld.conf` shipped by OCaml 5.5.0, was closed in favor of the more complete normalization implemented in [#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)
- The merge of **"Install cmx files to avoid warning 58"** ([#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120)) also closed the underlying issue report ([#117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/117)) from [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai)
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion converged on consolidating several path-handling and Windows-build PRs into a single relocatable-install effort.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#119](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/119), [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) noted that making `ld.conf` paths absolute without normalization could cause issues for systems where ocamlfind rewrites `ld.conf`, and pointed to a commit in [#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122) that handles both the absolute-path conversion and the normalization; [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai) agreed to close [#119](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/119) in favor of that consolidated implementation
- On [#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120), [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) explained the history behind several stale build artifacts being removed, noting `num_top` was never built for native code and that `ocaml_args.cmi` should not have been installed as far back as [#8](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/8), since `ocaml_args` is part of the `ocamlfind` binary rather than a library
- On [#121](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/121), [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) described removing legacy `mingw_lib`/`pure_mingw` handling determined to relate only to pre-MSYS2 environments, and moving `read_ldconf` from the `Frontend` module into `Findlib` so it can be tested in CI
repositories.trends_summary: Work is converging on a single relocatable-install branch for OCaml 5.5, consolidating several smaller path- and Windows-build PRs.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Several independently opened PRs addressing `ld.conf` path handling and Windows builds ([#119](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/119), [#112](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/112)) are being **consolidated** into the broader relocatable-install effort in [#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122), reducing the number of parallel code paths for the same underlying problem
- Continued **removal of legacy/dead build artifacts** — unused `.cmx` references, pre-MSYS2 mingw handling, and now proposed removal of `-with-relative-paths-at` ([#123](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/123)) — as the build is adapted for OCaml 5.5 and relocatable installs

repositories.contributors:

repositories.brief_summary: Pointer Capture and Lwt_js_events API completions merged; wasm linear-memory consolidation, Web Audio bindings, and an ESM RFC advance in review.
repositories.new_features_summary: Pointer Capture API bindings and a widened Lwt_js_events element type landed on master this week (#2403, #2404).
repositories.new_features:
- Pointer Capture API support added to `Dom_html.element` — `setPointerCapture`, `releasePointerCapture`, and `hasPointerCapture` — plus the previously missing `pointerEvent` members `getPredictedEvents`, `altitudeAngle`, and `azimuthAngle` (Pointer Events level 3 stylus tilt), by [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) ([#2403](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2403))
- `Lwt_js_events` `load`/`error`/`abort` and their `seq_loop` variants (`loads`/`errors`/`aborts`) now accept any `#Dom_html.element` instead of being restricted to `imageElement`, so waiting on a `<script>`, `<link>`, `<iframe>` or media element's load event no longer needs the low-level `Lwt_js_events.make_event` workaround, by [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) ([#2404](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2404))
repositories.activity_summary: New PR consolidates wasm linear memory for Safari (#2405); Web Audio, ESM RFC, and wasm lifecycle work continue in review (#2401, #2402, #2232).
repositories.activity:
- A newly opened PR from [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) consolidates the wasm runtime's four separate **linear memories** — the `jsstring.wat` scratch buffer, the separately-linked zstd and blake2 implementations, and the wasi libc memory — into a single shared memory, needed because Safari does not support wasm modules with multiple memories ([#2405](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2405))
- The Pointer Capture/`pointerEvent` bindings ([#2403](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2403)) and `Lwt_js_events` element-type widening ([#2404](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2404)) opened by [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) both merged this week
- [Hugo Heuzard](https://github.com/hhugo) continues work on **Web Audio and Media Capture API bindings** — `AudioContext`/`OfflineAudioContext`, the full audio node graph (sources, filters, panners, analyser), `MediaStream`/`MediaStreamTrack`, `navigator.mediaDevices`, and completion of `Dom_html.mediaElement` (text tracks, `srcObject`, playback-quality) — still open for review ([#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401))
- [Hugo Heuzard](https://github.com/hhugo) also keeps iterating on the draft **experimental ES module output** RFC, adding an `--esm` mode to `compile`/`build-runtime`/`link` and comparing bundled vs. unbundled linking size and speed tradeoffs to inform the ESM design discussions in [#1161](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1161) and [#551](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/551) ([#2402](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2402))
- [Jason Gross](https://github.com/JasonGross)'s PR to dispatch `wasmoocaml:loaded`/`wasmoocaml:error` **lifecycle events** when asynchronous Wasm instantiation completes remains open, with discussion this week narrowing a CI failure down to an unrelated opam package download flake rather than the change itself ([#2232](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2232))
repositories.discussions_summary: balat traced a wasm-only 'bad cast' trap to an untyped FFI read pattern that works under the JS backend but traps under wasm (#2406).
repositories.notable_discussions: - [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) opened and then personally root-caused a wasm-only **"bad cast"** trap ([#2406](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2406)): initially suspected to be a Firefox- or JSPI-specific engine bug, the trap was traced instead to an untyped `Js.Unsafe.coerce` FFI read in a downstream ocsigen-toolkit function whose result was inferred as OCaml `int` — a pattern that traps under wasm whenever the underlying JS number is fractional (e.g. `pageYOffset` on a scrolled page at a fractional/hidpi device pixel ratio), while working silently under the JS backend; the fix landed in [ocsigen/ocsigen-toolkit#271](https://github.com/ocsigen/ocsigen-toolkit/pull/271), and the thread flags the general hazard — any `Js.Unsafe.coerce` read inferred as `int`/`bool`/`float` is a latent value-dependent wasm trap — as worth documenting in the wasm_of_ocaml FFI docs
repositories.trends_summary: Work continues to expand typed Web-platform bindings and harden the wasm backend for cross-browser correctness (#2401, #2403, #2405, #2406).

repositories.brief_summary: Unsigned division primitives, a safe effects API, and DWARF debugging groundwork landed alongside continued flambda2/typing cleanup.
repositories.new_features_summary: Unsigned divmod primitives, a safe effects API, alloc_regions, and new -ddebug-avail-sets/-gdwarf-compression compiler flags.
repositories.new_features:
- Added **unsigned division and remainder primitives** (e.g. `%int64#_unsigned_div`, `%int64#_unsigned_mod`) for native and bytecode, and rewired `Int8`/`Int8_u`/`Int16`/`Int16_u`'s `unsigned_div`/`unsigned_rem` onto them, by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#4936](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/4936))
- Added a **"safe" effects API** requiring a local, yielding `Handler.t` phantom value to perform effects, so it is impossible (short of silencing alerts) to perform an effect from an unyielding context, by [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) ([#6281](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6281))
- Added **`Dynamic`** to the Stdlib, exposing the dynamics implementation previously only used internally by the test suite, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6412](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6412))
- Added **`alloc_regions`** to `alloc_modes` and threaded it through every allocating primitive as groundwork for future zero-alloc-with-regions checking (no checking performed yet), by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6121](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6121))
- Allowed **definition of atomic fields in mixed records** (use is still prohibited pending field-offset support), by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([#6423](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6423))
- Added **`float32_u`** to the predef types as `type float32_u = float32#`, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6459](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6459))
- Added **attributes on module aliases in signatures**, by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#5869](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5869))
- New **`-ddebug-avail-sets`** dump flag prints register-availability sets when dumping Linear/CFG, part of the ongoing `dwarf202607` DWARF-debugging series, by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6511](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6511))
- **`-gdwarf-compression`** now also applies to standard `-g` DWARF output rather than only `-gdwarf-inlined-frames`/`-gno-upstream-dwarf` builds, by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([#6490](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6490))
- Distinguished **language constructs that cannot be stack-allocated** (constants, things not-yet-supported, and genuinely non-allocating expressions) in the stack-allocation analysis, by [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn) ([#6471](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6471))
- Fixed **`-short-paths` error printing** so it no longer emits spurious "has no unboxed version" errors, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6458](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6458))
- Fixed **3 CFG peephole bugs**, including a potential miscompilation from integer overflow when simplifying a `mul`/`lsl` sequence, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6424](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6424))
- Fixed a **CSE bug** where the CFG pass hoisted mutable loads across atomic loads/fences, satisfying them with an equation from before the barrier, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6433](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6433))
- Fixed **missing `CFI_SIGNAL_FRAME`** annotations in `caml_do_call_gc`, `caml_preempt`, and `caml_call_gc` on amd64/arm64, which had been breaking gdb backtraces starting inside the GC, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6456](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6456))
- Linking programs that use metaprogramming no longer leaves stray `bundled_cm` assembly/object files in the temp directory, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6492](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6492))
- Compilation units loaded from a plain `-I` directory (rather than `-Ix`, which guarantees a `.cmx`) are now forced to **dynamic staticity**, with a hint pointing users at `-Ix`, by [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn) ([#6226](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6226))
- Converted remaining `_exn`-suffixed functions left over from the OCaml 5.4 merge to the newer `_res`/`caml_result` convention, by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#6411](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6411))
- Defunctionalized the `%resume` primitive, which previously drove `continue`/`discontinue`/`discontinue_with_backtrace` via a shared function/argument pair, by [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) ([#6440](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6440))
- Fixed a **dead documentation link** in the kinds-syntax reference page, by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#6463](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6463))
- Improved the **test-output normalizer** to strip fragile LLDB closure-value output rather than requiring per-machine promotion, by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#6464](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6464))

repositories.discussions_summary: Review threads probed nested zero_alloc_ annotation handling, Merlin typing-recovery removal risk, and allocation-mode axis fixes for partial application.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- Review of [Dmitrii Kalinichenko](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js)'s new `zero_alloc_` keyword ([#6537](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6537)) surfaced correctness concerns from [@zhizhuoxin](https://github.com/zhizhuoxin) about nested `zero_alloc_` annotations splitting incorrectly at the first zero-alloc lock, and about `statefulness` being set alongside the allocation axis when it should not affect other mode axes
- On [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw)'s PR adding the Merlin typing-recovery mechanism directly into the type checker ([#6366](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6366)), [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) pushed back on dropping recovery logic already present in oxcaml-merlin without first understanding why it existed, and flagged tests that need promotion or are raising fatal errors
- [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn)'s allocation-mode axis fix for multi-argument functions and partial application ([#6452](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6452)) saw detailed back-and-forth with [@zhizhuoxin](https://github.com/zhizhuoxin) over how `post_mode` and `pp_desc` should behave when walking locks under a noalloc closure lock, ending with a temporary hack being removed after review
- [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark)'s PR recording unyielding calls in bytecode debug events ([#6251](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6251)) drew review requests from [Dmitrii Kalinichenko](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) for additional test coverage of `unyielding-call(2)` generation and functors with mixed yielding/unyielding arguments

repositories.brief_summary: A potential double-free in `io_uring_queue_init` error handling was reported and investigated, then closed as not a bug ([#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160)).
repositories.activity_summary: The week's activity centered on a single issue reporting and resolving a suspected double-free in the C stubs ([#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160)).
repositories.activity:
- A potential **double-free vulnerability** in the error path of `io_uring_queue_init_params` was reported by [Vesa Karvonen](https://github.com/polytypic), who observed that `ring` is freed with `caml_stat_free` on initialization failure while the custom block backing `v_uring` could also free it later via its finalizer ([#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160))
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) investigated the report and closed the issue after confirming that `v_uring`'s finalizer is `custom_finalize_default`, which is `NULL`, so the GC does not actually attempt a second free of `ring` ([#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160))
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion on #160 examined whether an AI-flagged double-free in the C stubs was a real bug, concluding it was not.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- The report on [#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160) was notable for being **spotted by AI during code review** rather than manual inspection, raising the question of a dangling pointer left in `ring` after a failed `io_uring_queue_init_params` call
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) resolved the discussion by pointing to the existing finalizer documentation in `uring_stubs.c` (lines 68-72), which explains why the custom block's `NULL` finalizer prevents any actual double free ([#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160))
repositories.trends_summary: AI-assisted code review is starting to surface subtle memory-safety questions in the project's C stubs.
repositories.emerging_trends: - Use of **AI-assisted code review** to flag potential memory-safety edge cases in the `uring_stubs.c` C bindings appeared this week, as noted explicitly in the report on [#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160)
repositories.contributors_summary: Two contributors were involved this week: one reporting a suspected memory-safety issue and one investigating and closing it.
repositories.contributors:
- [Vesa Karvonen](https://github.com/polytypic) reported a potential double-free in the `io_uring_queue_init` error-handling path, identified with the assistance of AI code review tooling ([#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160))
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) reviewed the report, cited the relevant finalizer code in `uring_stubs.c`, and closed the issue after clarifying that no double free actually occurs ([#160](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/160))

repositories.brief_summary: Eio advanced v1.4 socket-option and io_uring work, reorganized eio_linux internals, and updated the changelog for release.
repositories.new_features_summary: macOS TCP_KEEPIDLE support, a new Eio_unix.Err module, and expanded io_uring use for sockets/fsync landed ahead of v1.4.
repositories.new_features:
- TCP_KEEPIDLE socket option support added for **macOS** by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), alongside disabling `TCP_FASTOPEN` on non-Linux platforms where it produced unreliable results ([#890](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/890)).
- New `Eio_unix.Err` module by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) exposes a public `Err.v` function for wrapping `Unix_error` exceptions as `Eio.Io` errors, replacing ad-hoc duplicated logic across `eio_linux`, `eio_posix`, and `eio_windows` ([#887](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/887)).
- `Eio_linux.Low_level` gained `socket`, `bind`, and `listen` functions with **io_uring** support, falling back to plain syscalls on older kernels, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) building on [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s work ([#884](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/884), [#850](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/850)).
- `Eio_linux.Low_level` also gained `ftruncate` and `fdatasync`, and now routes `fsync`/`shutdown` through io_uring, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm); a new `Eio.Exn.Not_available` exception was added for operations unsupported on a given backend ([#850](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/850)).
- Socket-option stubs were moved into `eio.unix` so extended options can be shared between `eio_linux` and `eio_posix` and implemented for other platforms, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#889](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/889)), followed by a fix ensuring sockopt functions always raise proper `Eio` exceptions instead of leaking a raw `Unix_error` ([#891](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/891)).
- Documentation fix for the `Unix_error` docstring in `eio_unix` by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#888](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/888)).
- `CHANGES.md` and library documentation updated to describe the accumulated **v1.4** feature set, including the `Sockopt` module, `Path.chmod`/`chown`, `Path.with_dir_entries`, and `Eio_unix.Pty`, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#892](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/892)).
repositories.activity_summary: A select()-fallback PR and pre-connect socket-option work remain open, while the sockopt refactor and eio_linux reorg merged.
repositories.activity:
- A new PR from [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) proposes falling back to `select()` for file descriptors where macOS's `poll()` incorrectly returns `POLLNVAL` (e.g. `/dev/tty`, `/dev/null`), fixing an assertion failure in `sched.ml` and following on from the discussion in [#757](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/757) ([#893](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/893)).
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) continues iterating on a **pre-connect socket options** design exposing a GADT-based options list for `bind_to` and socket setup, building on [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w)'s earlier work and simplified after discussion with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/875), [#713](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/713)), plus an open proposal to add an `SO_TYPE` query to the portable socket interface ([#860](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/860)).
- The **socket-option** refactor landed in stages: moving stubs into `eio.unix` for cross-backend sharing ([#889](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/889)), fixing a regression so sockopt functions always raise `Eio` exceptions ([#891](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/891)), and adding macOS `TCP_KEEPIDLE` support alongside cross-platform option testing on macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD ([#890](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/890)), all by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5).
- **eio_linux** internals were reorganized to mirror the `eio_posix` layout, splitting `net.ml`, `process.ml`, `fs.ml`, and `time.ml` out of the monolithic backend module by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#886](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/886)), building on the addition of uring-backed `Low_level.{socket,bind,listen}` ([#884](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/884)) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s `ftruncate`/`fdatasync`/uring `fsync`/`shutdown` work ([#850](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/850)).
- Cleanup work removed all remaining uses of `[@@@alert "-unstable"]`, a workaround for an old Merlin bug no longer needed ([#885](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/885)), deleted leftover test files after test runs ([#883](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/883)), and added braces around a switch case to silence a compiler warning, contributed by [Olaf Hering](https://github.com/olafhering) ([#882](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/882)).
- Release preparation continued with the **v1.4** changelog and documentation update summarizing breaking changes (`Net.getaddrinfo` now raises on error rather than returning `[]`) and the full set of new features merged over recent weeks, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#892](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/892)).
repositories.discussions_summary: Cross-platform socket-option testing surfaced platform quirks, and a report of high IO pressure on an idle io_uring service.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Marijan Petričević](https://github.com/marijanp) raised a question about persistently high `iowait`/IO pressure reported by the kernel for an otherwise idle Eio io_uring-backed service, despite no visible disk activity or blocked processes ([#862](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/862)).
- Cross-platform testing results shared on [#890](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/890) showed several "Linux-only" socket options also work on macOS and Windows, and surfaced a likely `errno`-message bug in FreeBSD's `tcp_usrreq.c` where `ESRCH` is reported as a process-not-found error, discussed by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm).
- On [#884](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/884), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) discussed design alternatives for tracking uring feature support, weighing storing the probe itself against per-feature booleans or a functor-based dispatch, and settled on storing the probe directly.
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) noted in [#885](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/885) that the removed `[@@@alert "-unstable"]` annotations dated back to a since-fixed Merlin bug ([ocaml/merlin#1558](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/1558)).
repositories.trends_summary: Consolidation of socket-option handling into a shared eio.unix layer and wider io_uring adoption continued across backends.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Continued consolidation of socket-option handling into a shared `eio.unix` layer so `eio_linux`, `eio_posix`, and eventually `eio_windows` reuse the same C stubs and exception handling ([#889](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/889), [#891](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/891), [#890](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/890), [#860](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/860), [#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/875)).
- Broader adoption of **io_uring** for operations previously done with plain syscalls, extending beyond reads/writes to `socket`, `bind`, `listen`, `shutdown`, and `fsync` ([#850](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/850), [#884](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/884)).
- `eio_linux` internals are being restructured to match the module layout already used in `eio_posix`, easing cross-backend maintenance ([#886](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/886)).
- Release housekeeping activity, including changelog updates, dead-code removal, and workaround cleanup, ahead of the v1.4 release ([#892](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/892), [#885](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/885), [#883](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/883)).
repositories.contributors_summary: avsm and talex5 drove uring/socket-option work and the eio_linux reorganisation; olafhering and marijanp each contributed once.
repositories.contributors:

- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) merged the sockopt exception fix ([#891](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/891)), macOS `TCP_KEEPIDLE` support with cross-platform testing ([#890](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/890)), the sockopt-stub relocation to `eio.unix` ([#889](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/889)), the new `Eio_unix.Err` module ([#887](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/887)), the `eio_linux` file split ([#886](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/886)), removal of the obsolete `[@@@alert "-unstable"]` workaround ([#885](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/885)), uring-backed `Low_level.{socket,bind,listen}` ([#884](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/884)), test-file cleanup ([#883](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/883)), and the v1.4 changelog/documentation update ([#892](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/892)); reviewed [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s uring PR ([#850](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/850)).
- [Olaf Hering](https://github.com/olafhering) contributed a code-cleanup fix adding braces around a switch-case block to resolve a compiler warning ([#882](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/882)).
- [Marijan Petričević](https://github.com/marijanp) reported an issue about high IO pressure observed for an idle io_uring-backed service ([#862](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/862)).

group_summaries.brief_summary: New opam-repository package submissions and riot's deprecation coincided with ocaml.org's opam version-page rework and docs-server proposal.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: New OCaml libraries (noise, wax, cascade, theo, termaid, cvc5) merged in opam-repository; only automated content merged on ocaml.org.
group_summaries.new_features:
- Initial release of **noise**, an implementation of the Noise Protocol Framework (revision 34), by [Race](https://github.com/raquentin) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30288](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30288))
- Initial release of **termaid**, an OCaml port of Rust's `mermaid.rs` renderer drawing Mermaid diagrams as Unicode box art, by [Alex Leighton](https://github.com/alexleighton) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30287](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30287))
- Initial release of **theo**, a BDD library with hash-consing, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30279](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30279))
- Initial release of **wax** (2 packages), a compiler toolchain for a Rust-like WebAssembly syntax, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30278](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30278))
- Initial release of **cascade**, a CSS generation library extracted from the `tw` (Tailwind CSS v4 in OCaml) project, by [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30280](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30280))
- Initial release of **cvc5** OCaml bindings for the cvc5 SMT solver, by [@filipeom](https://github.com/filipeom) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30289](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30289))
- **ochre**/**ochre-cli** 1.1.0 merged with built-in plaintext/text/txt language support, by [David Sancho](https://github.com/davesnx) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30265](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30265))
- **digestif** 1.3.1 and **mimic** 0.0.10 merged with improved protocol-instantiation error messages, by [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30268](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30268), [ocaml/opam-repository#30269](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30269))
- **melange** 7.0.1 merged, fixing incorrect relocation of relative `mel.module` externals during inlining, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30253](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30253))
- **dap** 1.1.0 merged with an updated Debug Adapter Protocol schema, by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30233](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30233))
- Automated **OCaml Planet** scraping merged new blog post entries into ocaml.org, including a post on static data race freedom in OxCaml and two OCaml Weekly News editions ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3711](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3711), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3715](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3715))
- No other code changes landed on ocaml.org's `main`; the opam package version page rework ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3713)) and docs-server switch ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3716](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3716)) remained open pending review
group_summaries.group_overview:
- **ocaml/opam-repository**: merged around a dozen package releases and processed a wave of brand-new library submissions spanning cryptography, WebAssembly, CSS tooling, and formal methods ([ocaml/opam-repository#30288](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30288), [ocaml/opam-repository#30280](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30280), [ocaml/opam-repository#30279](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30279))
- All versions of the **riot** package were marked non-maintained and unavailable after bad checksums were reported ([ocaml/opam-repository#30252](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30252), fixing [ocaml/opam-repository#30242](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30242))
- **ocaml/ocaml.org**: no code merged to `main` beyond automated Planet content scraping ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3711](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3711)); two substantive PRs reworking the opam version-status page and switching documentation links remained under review ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3713), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3716](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3716))
- Group activity centered on expanding the package ecosystem in opam-repository, while ocaml.org's open work focused on presenting that ecosystem's version data more accurately to end users
group_summaries.activity_summary: Package releases and OCaml 5.5 compatibility work in opam-repository ran alongside new PRs on ocaml.org's opam version pages and doc links.
group_summaries.activity:
- opam-repository processed numerous newly opened package submissions covering formal methods and scientific tooling, including **lstar-rocq** ([ocaml/opam-repository#30291](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30291)) by [Charles Averill](https://github.com/CharlesAverill), **gmp** 6.3.0-1 with new DragonFly BSD support ([ocaml/opam-repository#30290](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30290)) by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm), and 8 packages previewing **opam 2.6.0~alpha1** ([ocaml/opam-repository#30284](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30284)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- OCaml 5.5 compatibility work continued in opam-repository, with a preview **ocamlfind** package addressing an `ld.conf` parsing failure ([ocaml/opam-repository#30285](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30285)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)
- **hegel** (property-based testing) and **GenArrayIter** (Bigarray multi-dimensional iteration) each iterated through several superseded revisions before merging at 0.12.0 and 0.3.1 respectively ([ocaml/opam-repository#30271](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30271), [ocaml/opam-repository#30262](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30262))
- On ocaml.org, [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto) opened a rework of the **opam package version status page**, replacing the recommendation-implying heading with neutral Latest/Previous/Not-normally-selected groupings and accessible status labels, in response to a forum report ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3713))
- [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) opened a switch of **documentation links** to a new docs server (`dill.caelum.ci.dev`) that distinguishes doc-build failures from dependency "cascade" failures, keeping the old server live as a fallback ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3716](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3716))
- [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder) continued preparing the **dune 3.24 release** announcement on ocaml.org, seeking review from Tarides colleagues ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3704](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3704))
- The automated **platform releases scraper** on ocaml.org remained open awaiting merge, tracking new OCaml Platform tool releases ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3693](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3693))
group_summaries.cross_repository_work:
- ocaml.org's opam package version-status page rework ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3713)) concerns how opam-repository's own package release and version data — the same packages merged and submitted this week, e.g. [ocaml/opam-repository#30265](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30265) — is presented to end users
- ocaml.org's automated **platform releases scraper** ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3693](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3693)) and its **dune 3.24 release** announcement ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3704](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3704)) track tooling releases that are published as packages through opam-repository
- No PRs or issues this week directly referenced both repositories; the connection between them remained at the ecosystem-data level rather than through shared commits or cross-linked issues
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) flagged bad checksums across `riot` 0.0.2-0.0.5 and 0.0.7 to upstream maintainer [Leandro Ostera](https://github.com/leostera) in opam-repository ([ocaml/opam-repository#30242](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30242)); the package was subsequently marked non-maintained ([ocaml/opam-repository#30252](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30252))
- A long-standing opam-repository discussion on adding `conf-make`, `conf-cc` and `conf-cpp` packages continued, with [Pau Ruiz Safont](https://github.com/psafont) raising GNU-make-vs-BSD-make cross-platform naming concerns ([ocaml/opam-repository#19478](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/19478))
- [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) explained the need for a version-bound on `ochre-cli.1.0.0` after `ochre.1.1.0` caused reverse-dependency test failures when combined with the older CLI version ([ocaml/opam-repository#30277](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30277))
- On ocaml.org, [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) and [Haochen M. Kotoi-Xie](https://github.com/haochenx) reviewed the opam version-page rework, raising concerns about incorrect documentation link targets and the risk of showing unreleased compiler versions as the latest official release; the thread converged on adding a disclaimer banner pointing to `ocaml.org/releases` ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3713))
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- **OCaml 5.5 compatibility** preparation is underway in opam-repository, including a preview `ocamlfind` package ([ocaml/opam-repository#30285](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30285)) and opam 2.6.0~alpha1 preview packages ([ocaml/opam-repository#30284](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30284))
- A cluster of **brand-new library submissions** rather than version bumps landed in opam-repository, spanning cryptography, CSS tooling, WebAssembly, and terminal rendering ([ocaml/opam-repository#30288](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30288), [ocaml/opam-repository#30280](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30280), [ocaml/opam-repository#30278](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30278))
- Growing attention to **accuracy of package/version metadata** shown to end users, seen in ocaml.org's opam version-page rework prompted by forum feedback ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3713)) and mirrored by opam-repository's own version-bound fix to prevent a broken package combination ([ocaml/opam-repository#30277](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30277))
- Package submissions with **multiple superseding revisions** before merge remain common in opam-repository, as seen with **hegel** and **GenArrayIter** ([ocaml/opam-repository#30271](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30271), [ocaml/opam-repository#30262](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30262))

group_summaries.brief_summary: Opam released 2.6.0~alpha1 with .install root/rootexec sections dune already targets, while dune hardened spawning and merlin shipped an LRU cache.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: Opam 2.6.0~alpha1 shipped .install root/rootexec sections; dune added macOS sandboxing; merlin, ocamlfind and js_of_ocaml shipped fixes.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **[ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam)** released **2.6.0~alpha1** ([ocaml/opam#7046](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7046)), bundling `.install` file `root`/`rootexec` sections for arbitrary-prefix installs by [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian) and [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) ([ocaml/opam#6938](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6938), fixes [ocaml/opam#6919](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6919)), a new `--ignore-available-on` option by [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian) ([ocaml/opam#6836](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6836)), and two disk-usage reductions by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([ocaml/opam#6440](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6440), [ocaml/opam#6906](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6906))
- **[ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune)** removed `(using melange 0.1)` support ahead of Dune language 3.25, a breaking change, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([ocaml/dune#14574](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14574)), and added a macOS `sandbox-exec` sandboxing backend by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([ocaml/dune#15500](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15500))
- **[ocaml/merlin](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin)** added a `--cache-size` flag bounding `ocaml-index` memory via an LRU cache, bumping the on-disk index format version, by [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) ([ocaml/merlin#2079](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/pull/2079))
- **[ocaml/ocamlfind](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind)** now installs `.cmx` files for its libraries, resolving warning 58 in downstream projects such as Rocq, authored by [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai) ([ocaml/ocamlfind#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120), fixes [ocaml/ocamlfind#117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/117))
- **[ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp)** fixed dynamic workspace-folder addition ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1747](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1747)), Dune promotion reference counting ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1746](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1746)), and workspace-symbol resolution for generated sources ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1742](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1742)), all by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- **[ocsigen/js_of_ocaml](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml)** merged Pointer Capture API bindings ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2403](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2403)) and widened `Lwt_js_events` to accept any `#Dom_html.element` ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2404](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2404)), both by [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat)
group_summaries.group_overview:
- **[ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune)**: removed Melange 0.1 support (breaking, 3.25) ([ocaml/dune#14574](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14574)), added a macOS `sandbox-exec` backend ([ocaml/dune#15500](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15500)), and ran a broad process-spawning hardening pass across macOS and Windows
- **[ocaml/merlin](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin)**: merged an LRU-cache indexing memory-usage improvement ([ocaml/merlin#2079](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/pull/2079)); Windows CI failures were traced to an upstream dune regression ([ocaml/merlin#2096](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2096), [ocaml/dune#15512](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15512))
- **[ocaml/ocamlfind](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind)**: merged a `.cmx`-file install fix ([ocaml/ocamlfind#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120)); relocatable-install and Windows-build PRs opened for OCaml 5.5 ([ocaml/ocamlfind#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122), [ocaml/ocamlfind#121](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/121))
- **[ocaml/odoc](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc)**: driver fixes and a configurable compile output path were opened by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([ocaml/odoc#1461](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1461), [ocaml/odoc#1462](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1462)); the OxCaml modes-rendering PR remained in detailed review ([ocaml/odoc#1454](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1454))
- **[ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam)**: released **2.6.0~alpha1** ([ocaml/opam#7046](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7046)) with `.install` `root`/`rootexec` sections, `--ignore-available-on`, and disk-usage reductions
- **ocaml/opam-file-format**: no recorded activity this week
- **ocaml-dune/spawn**: no recorded activity this week
- **[ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp)**: shipped workspace-folder, Dune-promotion, and Dune-only-formatting fixes ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1747](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1747), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1746](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1746), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1621](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1621)) and completed a large TypeScript-to-OCaml end-to-end test migration ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1726](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1726))
- **[ocsigen/js_of_ocaml](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml)**: merged Pointer Capture and `Lwt_js_events` API completions ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2403](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2403), [ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2404](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2404)); opened a wasm linear-memory consolidation for Safari compatibility ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2405](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2405))
group_summaries.activity_summary: Dune hardened process spawning; ocaml-lsp migrated e2e tests off TypeScript; ocamlfind converged on relocatable installs.
group_summaries.activity:
- **[ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune)**: [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) landed a broad **process-spawning hardening** pass — workers now connect to the action-runner over an inherited socketpair ([ocaml/dune#15530](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15530)), plus fixes for macOS `chdir` error reporting ([ocaml/dune#15526](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15526)), fd-count tracing errors ([ocaml/dune#15529](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15529)), and `sendfile`/`wait4`/`fsevents` bugs ([ocaml/dune#15554](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15554), [ocaml/dune#15524](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15524), [ocaml/dune#15525](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15525)) — and continued a **package-management refactor** centralizing solver-environment composition, pin collection, and opam build-command generation ([ocaml/dune#15541](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15541), [ocaml/dune#15540](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15540), [ocaml/dune#15555](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15555), [ocaml/dune#15550](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15550)); [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder) handed off 3.24.1 release duties before a two-week absence and opened draft specs for the tools-management redesign ([ocaml/dune#15439](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15439), [ocaml/dune#15543](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15543), [ocaml/dune#13457](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13457))

group_summaries.brief_summary: oxcaml/oxcaml added unsigned division primitives, a safe effects API, and DWARF groundwork; opam-repository shipped five new compiler releases.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: Unsigned divmod primitives, a safe effects API, and DWARF flags landed in oxcaml/oxcaml; five compiler releases shipped in opam-repository.
group_summaries.new_features:
- Added **unsigned division and remainder primitives** (e.g. `%int64#_unsigned_div`, `%int64#_unsigned_mod`) for native and bytecode, rewiring `Int8`/`Int8_u`/`Int16`/`Int16_u` onto them, by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#4936](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/4936))
- Added a **"safe" effects API** requiring a local, yielding `Handler.t` phantom value to perform effects, making it impossible (short of silencing alerts) to perform an effect from an unyielding context, by [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6281](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6281))
- Added **`alloc_regions`** to `alloc_modes`, threaded through every allocating primitive as groundwork for future zero-alloc-with-regions checking, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6121](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6121))
- Allowed **definition of atomic fields in mixed records** (use still prohibited pending field-offset support), by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6423](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6423))
- Added **`Dynamic`** to the Stdlib, exposing the dynamics implementation previously internal to the test suite, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6412](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6412))
- Added **`float32_u`** to the predef types as `type float32_u = float32#`, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6459](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6459))
- New **`-ddebug-avail-sets`** dump flag prints register-availability sets when dumping Linear/CFG, part of the ongoing `dwarf202607` DWARF-debugging series, by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6511](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6511))
- **`-gdwarf-compression`** now also applies to standard `-g` DWARF output rather than only inlined-frame builds, by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6490](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6490))
- Fixed **3 CFG peephole bugs**, including a potential miscompilation from integer overflow in a `mul`/`lsl` simplification, and a **CSE bug** hoisting mutable loads across atomic fences, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6424](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6424), [oxcaml/oxcaml#6433](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6433))
- Fixed **missing `CFI_SIGNAL_FRAME`** annotations in GC entry points on amd64/arm64, which had been breaking gdb backtraces starting inside the GC, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6456](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6456))
- oxcaml/opam-repository added **five new oxcaml-compiler releases** (5.2.0minus-38/39/40 bundling Jane Street 130.100+614 and 130.106+341, plus 5.4.0-ox1/ox2 previews), closing the long-standing request to bump the repository to 130.100+614, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27-js) ([oxcaml/opam-repository#54](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/pull/54), [oxcaml/opam-repository#46](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/46))

group_summaries.new_features:

- `caml_program` is now generated as a **loop over a table of module entry points** instead of one call block per module, making startup code size independent of the number of linked modules, by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) and Pierre Oechsel ([ocaml/ocaml#13217](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13217))
- Fixed `-dtypedtree` output incorrectly printing `Twith_modtypesubst` as `Twith_modtype`, by [Corentin De Souza](https://github.com/fantazio) ([ocaml/ocaml#14932](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14932))
- Documentation for `Gc.stat` corrected to state that `stack_size` (unlike `heap_chunks`, `free_blocks`, and `largest_free`) is now populated again in OCaml 5.5, by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([ocaml/ocaml#14942](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14942))

group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- Whether **functional record updates that implicitly copy atomic fields** should be forbidden or should perform an implicit atomic read: [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported the missing atomic load ([ocaml/ocaml#14918](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14918)); [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) opened a PR to forbid the pattern citing OxCaml's precedent ([ocaml/ocaml#14931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14931)), but after further discussion with [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli), and [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) concluded that record updates are more constrained than pattern-matching (fields are read exactly once, unconditionally), so [ocaml/ocaml#14931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14931) was closed in favor of [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)'s alternative that implicitly performs the atomic read ([ocaml/ocaml#14935](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14935))
- A related question on the **unspecified evaluation order** of fields in `{ r with ... }` record-update expressions, raised by [Guillaume Bury](https://github.com/Gbury), which [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) linked to the atomic-field discussion above ([ocaml/ocaml#14129](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14129), [ocaml/ocaml#14918](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14918), [ocaml/ocaml#14931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14931))
- [Michael Neumann](https://github.com/mneumann)'s request for point-free `{Option,Result}.andthen`/`orelse` combinators was closed by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli), who explained the stdlib team's preference for a `try_value`-style combinator (previously discussed in [ocaml/ocaml#13937](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13937)) over `andthen`/`orelse`, after which Neumann agreed and opened [ocaml/ocaml#14941](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14941) implementing `try_value` ([ocaml/ocaml#14893](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14893))
- [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) raised that `Gc.Memprof` does not track the lifetime of **bigarray subarrays**, causing memory-profiling tools like memtrace to underestimate live memory in applications such as Mirage ([ocaml/ocaml#14938](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14938))
- [Sebastian Pop](https://github.com/sebpop) and [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) debated whether the PLDI'18 *Bounding Data Races in Space and Time* compilation scheme's fences around AArch64 atomic RMWs are stronger than necessary, backed by herd7 litmus tests distinguishing LSE and LL/SC atomic forms ([ocaml/ocaml#14936](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14936))
- [Chet Murthy](https://github.com/chetmurthy) reported that `Scanf.unescaped` accepts hex (`\x41`) but rejects octal (`\o101`) escapes, which [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) confirmed matches the documented spec but agreed is surprising behavior ([ocaml/ocaml#14930](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14930))

group_summaries.new_features:
- TCP_KEEPIDLE socket option support added for **macOS** by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), alongside disabling `TCP_FASTOPEN` on non-Linux platforms where it produced unreliable results ([ocaml-multicore/eio#890](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/890)).
- New `Eio_unix.Err` module by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) exposes a public `Err.v` function for wrapping `Unix_error` exceptions as `Eio.Io` errors, replacing ad-hoc duplicated logic across `eio_linux`, `eio_posix`, and `eio_windows` ([ocaml-multicore/eio#887](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/887)).
- `Eio_linux.Low_level` gained `socket`, `bind`, and `listen` functions with **io_uring** support, falling back to plain syscalls on older kernels, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) building on [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s work ([ocaml-multicore/eio#884](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/884), [ocaml-multicore/eio#850](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/850)).
- `Eio_linux.Low_level` also gained `ftruncate` and `fdatasync`, and now routes `fsync`/`shutdown` through io_uring, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm); a new `Eio.Exn.Not_available` exception was added for operations unsupported on a given backend ([ocaml-multicore/eio#850](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/850)).
- Socket-option stubs were moved into `eio.unix` so extended options can be shared between `eio_linux` and `eio_posix`, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#889](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/889)), followed by a fix ensuring sockopt functions always raise proper `Eio` exceptions instead of leaking a raw `Unix_error` ([ocaml-multicore/eio#891](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/891)).
- `CHANGES.md` and library documentation updated to describe the accumulated **v1.4** feature set, including the `Sockopt` module, `Path.chmod`/`chown`, `Path.with_dir_entries`, and `Eio_unix.Pty`, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#892](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/892)).

group_summaries.cross_repository_work:
